arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Lawrence Lessig argued the extension exceeds congressional power. He cited First Amendment violations.
Theodore Olson argued the first Congress protected existing copyrights. He cited historical precedent for the extension.
Chief Justice Rehnquist introduced the case. He noted the how the case got here of the dispute.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The case tests the limits of copyright law. It asks if Congress can extend terms for existing works. The outcome affects public access to creative material.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: the sides that brought the case want the court to strike down the 1998 Act. They seek to restore public domain access to older works.
the opposing sides want the court to uphold the 1998 Act. They seek to maintain extended copyright protection for existing works.
